subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` keys that look like credentials be allowed into skill-owned host `exec` subprocesses, and what scoping prevents those secrets from leaking into unrelated exec calls?
rationale: The current source violates documented host skill-env behavior for affected users, but changing it decides when credential values may enter executable child-process environments.

options.title: Allow skill-scoped credential env
options.body: Permit user-configured per-skill env keys for that skill's own host exec context while keeping dangerous env names blocked and stripping skill secrets from unrelated generic exec.

options.title: Require metadata declarations
options.body: Keep credential-shaped names blocked unless the skill manifest declares them, then update `gog` metadata or docs for `GOG_KEYRING_PASSWORD`.

options.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
options.body: Document that credential-shaped per-skill env names are intentionally blocked and require top-level or system environment configuration.

recommendation.title: Allow skill-scoped credential env
recommendation.body: Permit user-configured per-skill env keys for that skill's own host exec context while keeping dangerous env names blocked and stripping skill secrets from unrelated generic exec.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses documented skill behavior, credential handling, and host exec security policy where steipete has the strongest product/security routing signal.
